The DOCX export in `act` uses two style matrices to control how transcripts
are rendered. Both matrices are stored in a single `.xlsx` file (sheets
`base` and `user`) or in separate `.csv` files.

# Base matrix (sheet `base`)

The base matrix maps act-internal style names to paragraph styles defined in
the `.docx` template file. Every layout object needs at least these five
styles:

| `act.style.name` | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `header.preface` | Preface line above the title |
| `header.title` | Transcript title |
| `header.subtitle` | Subtitle |
| `header.info` | Description / source information |
| `transcript.default` | Default paragraph style for annotations |

Additional styles can be added and referenced from the user matrix.

Use `act::export_styles_base_load()` to load the base matrix.

# User matrix (sheet `user`)

The user matrix defines per-tier formatting rules. Each row is a rule that
matches tiers by regex or layers by column name. The first matching rule
wins.

Use `act::export_styles_user_load()` to load the user matrix.

## Columns

### Identification

Each row must have at least one of the following:

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | Character | Human-readable label (informational only). |
| `tier.regex` | Character | Regex matched against tier names. First match wins. |
| `layer.name` | Character | Column name in the `annotations` data.frame to match as a layer. |

### Visibility

| Column | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `show` | Logical | `TRUE` | Render the tier/layer (`TRUE`) or hide it (`FALSE`). |

### Paragraph style

| Column | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docx.template.name` | Character | (transcript default) | Paragraph style name from the `.docx` template. |

### Line numbers

| Column | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `line.nr.show` | Logical | `TRUE` | Show line numbers (`TRUE`) or replace with spaces (`FALSE`). |

### Speaker acronym

| Column | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `acronym.show` | Logical | `TRUE` | Show (`TRUE`) or hide (`FALSE`) the speaker acronym. |
| `acronym.case` | Character | (no change) | Case transformation. Allowed: `toupper`, `tolower`, `capitalize`. |
| `acronym.search` | Character | -- | Regex search pattern applied to the acronym. |
| `acronym.replace` | Character | -- | Replacement string for `acronym.search` matches. |
| `acronym.width` | Numeric | `0` | Fixed character width (padded/truncated). `0` = global layout default. |
| `acronym.ending` | Character | (layout default) | String appended after the acronym (e.g., `:`). |

### Indentation (layers)

| Column | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content.indent` | Character | `none` | Indentation mode for layer lines. See below. |
| `content.indent.skip` | Character | -- | Regex for characters at the start of content to skip when calculating indent (only for `content.indent = "content"`). |
| `content.align.char` | Character | -- | Characters used as alignment target for `content.indent = "align"`. |

**Indentation modes** (`content.indent`):

| Value | Layer indented to ... |
|---|---|
| `none` | No indentation (column 0). |
| `linenumber` | Start of the line number. |
| `speaker` | Start of the speaker acronym. |
| `textblock` | Start of the text (after speaker + ending). |
| `content` | First non-whitespace character in the text. Use `content.indent.skip` to skip leading symbols. |
| `align` | Position of the first occurrence of any character in `content.align.char` within the main text. Falls back to `textblock` if not found. |

### Spacing

| Column | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `space.after` | Character | `NA` | Controls spacing after this tier's annotations. |

**`space.after` values:**

| Value | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `block` | Insert an empty paragraph after the end of the block (after the last visible line that belongs to the same main annotation). This is the typical setting for transcript tiers. |
| `always` | Insert an empty paragraph after every line of this tier, even if more lines in the same block follow. |
| `no` | No spacing after this tier. |

The empty paragraphs use a dedicated spacer paragraph style. A "block" is
defined as a main tier annotation together with all layer tier annotations
that follow it before the next main tier annotation.

### Other

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `comment` | Character | Free-text comment (ignored by the code). |

# Example

A minimal user matrix with three rules:

| name | show | tier.regex | layer.name | docx.template.name | line.nr.show | acronym.show | content.indent | space.after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Main | TRUE | `^(?!.*=)` | | | TRUE | TRUE | | block |
| Translation | TRUE | | translation | transcript_translation | FALSE | FALSE | content | block |
| Cut | TRUE | `^cut` | | transcript_transition | FALSE | FALSE | | always |

This configuration:

- Shows all tiers not containing `=` as main tiers with line numbers and speaker acronyms.
- Shows the `translation` layer without line numbers or acronyms, indented to the content position.
- Shows cut markers with a different paragraph style, with spacing before and after.

```r
# Load the styles
styles_base <- act::export_styles_base_load("my_styles.xlsx")
styles_user <- act::export_styles_user_load("my_styles.xlsx")

# Assign to layout
l <- methods::new("layout")
l@docx.styles.base <- styles_base
l@docx.styles.user <- styles_user
```
